pass_a_gloss: Logos 2. [Lemma, Isaiah 44:2:] Thus says the Lord God, the one who made you, and the one who formed you from belly: You will yet be helped. Having charged those from Israel with the apostasy, and with departing from the love toward him, and with assigning themselves to the gods that are not; for he said that, Your fathers and your rulers acted lawlessly against me, and the rulers defiled my holy things; most providentially he adds these things too; for he does not allow them to be carried off toward apostasy, or despair, nor yet to slip off wholly from the hope in him. And he announces gentleness to them again, and wins them back through the customary loving-kindness, and brings back toward change of mind. And he gives to understand that he has not wholly turned away from those who have sinned, nor yet will Israel perish root and all, he pitying, and making very smooth the way of salvation for those who believe in him; and saying himself to be Lord and God, having made and formed from belly, he seems to hint that he also strayed, having put the name of the godhead around others, and having fastened unthinkingly the glory of the lordship on the gods that are not. And that he also did not know the Maker, and the one who brought into existence the man on the earth, not being ever, he hints again, affirming himself to be former and maker, and as it were indicting for ingratitude those who leapt away from the love toward him. For indeed it is among absurd things that to the parents according to flesh the highest honours be brought by us, the divine law awarding this too, but that the generator of all not rather than those be honoured with the praises fitting him and be honoured by us through the complete submission. Some such thing he says also through one of the holy prophets: A son glorifies the father, and a slave his lord. And if I am father, where is my glory? And if I am lord, where is my fear? says the Lord Almighty. For he is in the same [person] both Lord, as having the whole creation under yokes and slavery. For the divine Melodist said somewhere to him that, All things are yours. And Father again as former and maker and having brought into being. So as in rank of debt one must lay down to God both the submission fitting sons and the fear suiting the household servants. So whenever former and maker himself [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Logos 2. 'Thus says the Lord God who made you and formed you from the womb: You will yet be helped' (Isaiah 44:2).

He had charged those of Israel with their apostasy, with drifting away from their love for him and giving themselves over to gods that do not exist; for he had said: 'Your fathers and your rulers have acted lawlessly against me, and the rulers have defiled my holy things' (Isaiah 43:27–28). Now, with great wisdom in his dealings with them, he adds these words as well. For he does not let them be carried off into apostasy, or rather into despair, nor slip away altogether from their hope in him. He promises them gentleness again, wins them back by his usual love for humankind, and brings them round to repentance.

He gives them to understand that he has not wholly turned away from those who have sinned, and that Israel will not perish root and branch, since he has pity on them and makes the way of salvation quite smooth for those who believe in him. In calling himself Lord and God, who made and formed Israel from the womb, he seems to hint that Israel has also gone astray by putting the name of divinity on others and thoughtlessly attaching the glory of lordship to gods that do not exist.

He hints again that Israel did not know his Maker, the one who brought the human being on earth into existence when he once did not exist; for he firmly declares that he himself is Former and Maker, and as it were charges with ingratitude those who have leapt away from their love for him. For it is absurd that we should offer the highest honors to our parents according to the flesh, the divine law also awarding them this (Exodus 20:12), and yet that the Creator of the universe should not, far more than they, be extolled by us with the praises fitting for him and honored by our complete submission.

He says something of this kind through one of the holy prophets too: 'A son honors his father, and a servant his lord. If then I am a father, where is my glory? And if I am Lord, where is the fear of me? says the Lord Almighty' (Malachi 1:6).

For he is both at once. He is Lord, as holding the whole creation under the yoke and in service; for the divine Psalmist said to him somewhere, 'All things are yours' (Psalm 119:91). And again he is Father, as Former and Maker, who brought it into being. So, as though paying a debt, we must render to God both the submission fitting for sons and the fear proper to household servants. So whenever he calls himself Former and Maker …
